title: Principal Applied AI Scientist, Commerce Foundation Models
job_description:
Principal Applied AI Scientist, Commerce Foundation Models

Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, ecommerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role

We’re looking for an experienced applied scientist to help set LCM’s research direction and work directly on its most demanding scientific problems. This is a hands-on individual contributor role in a flat team of around 30 engineers, with no direct reports. You will mentor colleagues and contribute to hiring, but you will not manage people.

We define how a capability will be evaluated before developing it, and use that evidence to guide training and deployment decisions. You will help decide which research questions deserve investment, design and run experiments, and develop training methods that can be used across applications.

The role requires deep expertise in a core area of model training and the judgment to connect that work with decisions about data, evaluation and deployment. Scientists and engineers work together from the first experiment through to production evaluation, and you will take scientific responsibility for agreed research projects.

A central research goal is to learn from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio and turn useful signals into regular updates to model weights.

What the role involves

-
Develop the research agenda with the team, identifying questions that affect model quality, training efficiency or downstream results. Use experiments to decide which approaches warrant larger training runs and which should be revised or stopped.

-
Lead selected research projects through implementation, training and evaluation, staying directly involved in writing code, inspecting data, debugging runs and analysing failures.

-
Establish evaluation methods that separate real improvements from leakage, noise and benchmark overfitting, and work with portfolio teams to test whether offline gains hold in controlled online experiments.

-
Mentor scientists and engineers through joint research, experiment reviews and technical discussion, and advise on work that crosses project boundaries.

-
Contribute to hiring, publish research and support the release of models, benchmarks and training methods where the work and data can be shared.

Research areas

The initial focus will depend on your expertise and the team’s priorities. We expect substantial depth in one of the two areas below, with the ability to contribute to decisions across the other.

Pre-training and representations

We continue pre-training open-weight models on commerce data. Research questions include how to represent users and catalogues, how to combine data from different businesses, and how to allocate compute effectively. Work may include:

-
Studying data mixtures, scaling behaviour and training schedules to guide the next run.

-
Designing sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, including alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants.

-
Developing mid-training methods for capability acquisition, context extension and retention of general capabilities.

-
Evaluating synthetic data and distillation methods through controlled experiments, including the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency.

-
Studying transfer across languages, markets and commerce categories, with evaluations for new users and items and for performance on future data.

-
Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation, including pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data.

Post-training and continual learning

We train LCM for commerce tasks and a range of agent applications, including customer-facing assistants and agents that carry out business operations. We also develop continual learning methods that turn new interactions into regular updates to model weights. Work may include:

-
Developing supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation and reinforcement learning methods, using verifiable outcomes or learned reward models.

-
Turning session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback into training examples and rewards, accounting for exposure bias, delayed feedback and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value.

-
Studying data selection, replay and update frequency so models learn from new interactions without losing established capabilities.

-
Training and evaluating decision models that choose rankings, offers and promotions, using offline learning and off-policy evaluation to estimate policy value and uncertainty and inform controlled online experiments.

-
Training models for multi-turn conversations and multi-step agent workflows, including understanding user intent, planning, tool use, maintaining context, recovering from errors and verifying outcomes. This includes building RL environments with simulated users and catalogues, and testing whether gains transfer to real interactions within defined permissions and business rules.

-
Calibrating reward models and LLM-based graders against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and investigating reward hacking and other unintended effects.

-
Developing automated experimentation methods that propose and test changes to training recipes, prompts, tools or agent control flow, with held-out evaluations and regression checks.

How we evaluate the work

Research should produce evidence that supports a training or deployment decision. We use strong baselines, including existing production systems, and weigh model quality against compute requirements, inference cost and latency.

Experiments should be reproducible, with ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis. They must account for temporal leakage, changes in the data distribution and differences between companies and markets. Negative results are valuable when they explain a limitation or stop further investment in an approach that does not work.

The work also involves data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories, together with our data and engineering teams.

In the first three months, we expect you to establish a focused research programme, resolve an important training or evaluation question, and work with the relevant teams to test the resulting method in a downstream application.

Minimum qualifications

-
A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field.

-
At least eight years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with at least four years leading research directions that were published or reached production.

-
Substantial experience developing and training models, with deep expertise in pre-training, post-training or reinforcement learning relevant to the areas above.

-
A record of original contributions, shown through research papers, released models, benchmarks, open-source projects or significant advances in deployed systems.

-
Scientific leadership: choosing research directions, resolving difficult technical questions and helping experienced colleagues make better decisions.

-
Sound experimental and statistical judgment, including examples where the evidence changed your approach and the ability to recognise when the evidence does not support a conclusion.

-
Strong Python and PyTorch skills and the ability to work independently in a shared research codebase. Research on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training.

-
Clear communication and a collaborative approach to disagreement, review and mentoring.

Preferred qualifications

-
Experience with recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs, continual learning, synthetic data, distillation or tabular foundation models.

-
Familiarity with commerce data and online experimentation.

-
We do not expect expertise in every area.

What we offer

-
Influence over LCM’s research agenda and which questions the team invests in.

-
Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking.

-
The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people.

-
Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

-
An uncapped budget to recruit and mentor research interns for your projects, with access to candidates through our connections with leading universities.

-
Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

-
A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

-
Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

How to apply

Please include examples of research or deployed work that show your contribution, the decisions involved and the evidence used to evaluate the results, and indicate which research area best matches your depth.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

title: Data Scientist, Trust & Safety
job_description:
Data Scientist, Trust & Safety

Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

You’ll join the Detection subdomain within Trust & Safety, whose mission is to protect the Vinted community by identifying harmful content and activities. We build detection capabilities that enable timely prevention and moderation, reducing members’ exposure to harm, while minimising disruption to legitimate members.

You’ll develop and improve machine learning models that identify harmful listings and suspicious behaviour across the marketplace, while minimising friction on legitimate members. Working with text, images and behavioural data, you’ll apply practical machine learning techniques to evolving detection challenges.

You’ll work closely with Data Scientists, Decision Scientists, Product Managers and engineers to turn ideas into reliable production solutions. You’ll take ownership of well-defined projects across the ML lifecycle, from understanding the data and developing models to deployment, evaluation and ongoing maintenance.

Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role

Evaluation is the core of everything we do. We build from the evals: we define how success will be measured before developing a capability, and use the results to guide training, model selection and deployment. We already have hundreds of evaluations spanning domain knowledge, commerce and gaming, with plans to expand their coverage, depth and scale.

This work builds on ProLLM, the public benchmarking platform we ran for real-world use cases until our coding assistant benchmarks became saturated. Since then it has been a private benchmarking platform for Prosus companies. We plan to open it again to publish our commerce benchmarks, covering both agentic and decision-making tasks.

We’re looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to own the development of these evaluations and the platform that runs them. The work involves defining meaningful tasks, curating evaluation data, implementing reliable scoring, investigating model behaviour and making results useful for research and product decisions.

In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work directly with applied scientists, training engineers and domain experts. You’ll help teams contribute evaluations and build the infrastructure and automation needed to run them throughout model development.

In the first three months, we expect you to take technical ownership of part of the evaluation platform, deliver a set of new or improved evaluations with curated data and calibrated difficulty, and work with scientists to use them in a training or release decision.

What the role involves

-
Design evaluations with scientists and domain experts, translating intended capabilities into representative tasks, datasets and success criteria. Cover current applications and capabilities we want future models to acquire.

-
Curate evaluation data and calibrate task difficulty, so that evaluations are neither saturated nor out of reach and still separate models of different quality. Work with domain experts on sourcing, annotation and review, within data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy requirements.

-
Own the development and operation of the evaluation platform across training checkpoints, deployed models and external baselines. Support distributed execution, reproducible configurations, trace inspection and comparison of results, while managing runtime and cost.

-
Develop programmatic checks, outcome-based scoring and LLM-based graders. Calibrate automated judgments against expert reviews, investigate disagreements and test whether graders reward superficial answers or reject valid solutions.

-
Analyse model outputs and agent trajectories, including tool calls, environment state and task outcomes. Distinguish model failures from problems in the evaluation, quantify uncertainty and explain what changed between versions.

-
Maintain versioned tasks, datasets, graders and environments, with protected held-out tests and contamination checks. Expand coverage as models improve, retaining useful regression tests and adding harder tasks where existing tests no longer distinguish performance.

-
Prepare commerce benchmarks for public release on ProLLM, including public mirror sets and evaluation code, where the data can be shared.

-
Integrate evaluations into training and release workflows, with dashboards and regression checks that support concrete decisions. Work with portfolio teams to establish whether offline improvements correspond to better outcomes in online experiments.

-
Build tools and agents that help generate candidate tasks, run evaluations and investigate failures, validating their outputs before adoption. Review contributions and mentor engineers so teams can extend the suite consistently.

Minimum qualifications

-
At least five years of ML or software engineering experience, including substantial hands-on work building and evaluating ML systems.

-
Experience owning evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or model-quality systems that informed training or deployment decisions.

-
Strong Python and experience with PyTorch, Transformers or comparable ML libraries, alongside reliable production software development.

-
Practical knowledge of experimental design and statistics, including sampling, uncertainty, repeated trials and comparisons across model versions.

-
Experience running inference or evaluation workloads at scale and debugging failures across models, data, scoring code and infrastructure.

-
Clear communication and the ability to turn ambiguous results into defensible recommendations.

Preferred qualifications

-
Experience with language-model training or post-training.

-
Experience with agent or gaming environments.

-
Experience with human evaluation, LLM-as-judge calibration, recommendation metrics or online experimentation.

-
Contributions to evaluation frameworks, public benchmarks or research.

What we offer

-
Ownership of the evaluation platform and the evaluations that guide LCM’s research, training and deployment.

-
Access to proprietary domain data, GPU infrastructure and external models for comparison.

-
Direct collaboration with researchers, engineers and portfolio teams, with scope to publish methods and benchmarks, including through ProLLM, where the work can be shared.

-
Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

-
Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

-
A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

-
Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

If you want to build the evaluations that shape what a foundation model learns, we’d like to hear from you. Please include examples of evaluations or platforms you have built, how you established that their results were reliable, and the decisions those results informed.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

title: Senior Applied AI Scientist, Commerce Foundation Models
job_description:
Senior Applied AI Scientist, Commerce Foundation Models

Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role

We’re looking for experienced applied scientists in two tracks: pre-training, and post-training and continual learning. Each scientist will own a focused research direction within a track. The areas below describe the team’s research agenda; we are looking for depth in one or more of them.

The role involves designing experiments, writing the code to run them, analysing results and developing training methods that other teams can use. Scientists own the research questions, training objectives and evidence needed to decide whether a change works, and work with ML engineers to turn successful experiments into reliable training runs. We are a team of around 30 engineers with a flat structure, working directly with portfolio companies to define problems, evaluate models and bring successful work into production.

In the first three months, the expectation is to establish strong baselines in a chosen research area, develop and evaluate an improvement, and work with the relevant teams to test it in a downstream application.

Track 1: Pre-training

This track focuses on continued pre-training of open-weight models on commerce data, including how we represent that data, allocate training compute and transfer capabilities to smaller models. Research areas include:

-
Studying scaling behaviour, data mixtures and compute allocation to decide what goes into the next training run.

-
Developing mid-training methods, including data refinement, annealing schedules, context extension and alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants.

-
Designing training sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, and studying how representations transfer across companies, languages and commerce categories.

-
Building synthetic data pipelines and measuring their contribution through controlled comparisons with real data.

-
Distilling the base model into smaller models, including through on-policy distillation, and measuring the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency.

-
Developing evaluations that help select pre-training runs and predict downstream performance, including checks for temporal leakage, generalisation to new users and items, and retention of existing capabilities.

-
Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation: pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data, using synthetic and real tables and comparing results with established tabular methods.

Relevant experience includes continued pre-training or mid-training, data mixture research, scaling laws, tokenisation, entity representations, distillation, or tabular foundation models such as TabPFN and TabICL.

Track 2: Post-training and continual learning

This track focuses on adapting LCM to commerce tasks and learning from interactions after deployment. The goal is to turn signals from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio into regular updates to model weights, while retaining the capabilities the model has already learned. Research areas include:

-
Developing post-training methods using supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation such as DPO, and reinforcement learning with verifiable or learned rewards, including GRPO and PPO.

-
Learning from session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback. This includes data selection, credit assignment and reward design that account for exposure bias, delayed outcomes and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value.

-
Studying how to combine new interactions with historical data, how frequently to update models, when an update is ready for deployment, and how to preserve performance as user behaviour and catalogues change.

-
Building RL environments with simulated users, catalogues and multi-step commerce tasks, including inspecting trajectories, validating rewards and testing whether improvements in simulation transfer to real interactions.

-
Developing reward models and LLM-based graders, calibrating them against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and testing for reward hacking, sycophancy and excessive concentration on popular items.

-
Training decision models for rankings, offers and promotions using contextual bandits or offline RL, with off-policy evaluation to estimate value and uncertainty, identify gaps in the available evidence and inform controlled online experiments.

-
Developing automated experiments that propose and test changes to training methods, prompts, tools or agent control flow, evaluated on held-out tasks and regression tests before acceptance.

Relevant experience includes language-model post-training, reinforcement learning, reward modelling, agent training environments, continual learning, or offline RL and bandits applied to real decisions. The training experience required will depend on the research direction.

Responsibilities across both tracks

-
Define success with portfolio teams and evaluate models against strong baselines, including existing production systems, accounting for inference cost, latency and the business outcome the model is meant to improve.

-
Design reproducible experiments with appropriate ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis, using future-period and held-out evaluations, and test whether offline improvements hold online.

-
Work with data and engineering teams on provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories.

-
Publish research and contribute models, benchmarks, environments and training methods to open source where the work and data can be shared.

-
Mentor colleagues, review experiment designs and communicate findings clearly enough to support training and deployment decisions.

Minimum qualifications

-
A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field.

-
At least five years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with hands-on experience designing and running model-training experiments. For Track 1, this should include pre-training or mid-training of language models. For Track 2, it should include language-model post-training, or reinforcement learning and decision-model training relevant to the specialisation.

-
Evidence of original research through papers, released models, public benchmarks, open-source projects or significant research contributions to deployed systems.

-
Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with experience implementing experiments and debugging training runs in a shared research codebase. Work on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training.

-
Sound experimental judgment, including strong baselines, statistical analysis and the willingness to report negative results.

-
Clear written and verbal communication.

Preferred qualifications

-
Experience implementing and debugging training methods in frameworks such as Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, NeMo RL, verl or OpenRLHF, depending on the chosen track.

-
Research in recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs or user behaviour modelling.

-
Experience with synthetic data, model distillation or compression for production.

-
Experience working with marketplace or commerce data and evaluating changes through online experiments.

What we offer

-
Autonomy to design experiments and make technical decisions within your research direction.

-
Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking.

-
The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people.

-
Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

-
An uncapped budget to recruit and mentor research interns for your projects, with access to candidates through our connections with leading universities.

-
Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

-
A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

-
Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

If you want to work on these problems, we would like to hear from you. Please indicate the track and research areas that best match your experience, and include examples of work that show your contribution.
